articles.title: Pandemic-Era Longing to Gather Fed Qiu Jiongjiong’s Tokyo Competition Title ‘Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting’
articles.summary: Chinese painter and filmmaker Qiu Jiongjiong began shaping his new film during the pandemic. With the world suddenly forced to pause, he tells Variety, people felt an urgent desire to return to everyday life and to gather around a table.
body: “This may be the film with the most dialogue I’ve ever had, but I couldn’t understand a word of it,” says Taiwanese star Lee Kang-sheng, the longtime lead of director Tsai Ming-liang’s films. He plays two elderly women from different eras, including a dying grandmother in the film’s prehistoric chapter. The entire film is spoken in the Leshan dialect of Sichuan province.

Lee Kang-sheng worked with several dialect coaches, Qiu says. “I was drawn to the mysterious quality about him, which felt perfectly suited to a character from ancient times,” he says. “That gave me the idea of asking him to play a woman.”

Taiwanese actor Lee Hong-chi, who also worked with dialect coaches, plays Song dynasty poet Su Dongpo. He had long admired Qiu’s visual work. “I only found out I was playing Su Dongpo when I got the script,” he says. “The dialect was a challenge for me, too, but I really wanted to be part of the film because of its nonrealistic aesthetic and the world Qiu had created.”

With the world suddenly forced to pause, he tells Variety, people felt an urgent desire to return to everyday life and to gather around a table.

articles.title: Judge Dismisses Trump’s Wall Street Journal Defamation Lawsuit Over Published Epstein ‘Birthday Book’ for a Second Time
articles.summary: A federal judge has once again dismissed President Donald Trump’s defamation claims against the Wall Street Journal over a 2025 report by the paper that a 2003 birthday letter to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was purportedly written by Trump.
body: In April, Judge Gayles ruled that the lawsuit “fails to adequately allege actual malice,” a legal standard in the U.S. for proving defamation. At the time, the court dismissed the complaint “without prejudice,” since he had only made one attempt to state his claims.

Trump sought at least $20 billion in damages on two counts of defamation in the initial suit, filed in July 2025. He sued the WSJ, its parent companies Dow Jones & Co. and News Corp, the reporters on the story and Rupert Murdoch.

“We have just filed a POWERHOUSE Lawsuit against everyone involved in publishing the false, malicious, defamatory, FAKE NEWS ‘article’ in the useless ‘rag’ that is, The Wall Street Journal,” Trump wrote at the time on Truth Social. “I hope Rupert and his ‘friends’ are looking forward to the many hours of depositions and testimonies they will have to provide in this case.”

articles.title: Tokyo Asian Future Drama ‘Jani Be Good’ Probes Silence and Motherhood in a Chinese-Indonesian Family, Marking Ariani Darmawan’s Return
articles.summary: Indonesian filmmaker Ariani Darmawan stepped away from directing for years to raise a family. Her first feature, “Jani Be Good,” which is playing in the Tokyo International Film Festival’s Asian Future competition, turns that experience into a portrait of four women across three generations.
body: Unfolding across four December days in the lead-up to Christmas, the film follows 13-year-old Jani after she overhears a fight between her 18-year-old sister Julia and their mother Winnie, and Julia leaves home. Winnie, a single mother who works as an accountant and fills fruit hamper orders on the side, grows short-tempered with the daughter who stayed. Jani, who has been secretly trading messages with Julia, leans on her grandmother, Oma, who makes spring rolls to sell so she can put money aside for her own cremation. The household is Chinese-Catholic.

The four leads are Chempa Puteri, Sigi Wimala, Tutie Kirana and Hyori Mika. Darmawan co-wrote the screenplay with Cyntha Hariadi. Taurisia produced for Palari Films, the Jakarta-based company she runs with fellow producer Muhammad Zaidy. Palari, founded in 2016, opens the film in Indonesian cinemas on Dec. 10.

articles.title: ‘Never big enough’: inside the booming penis enlargement industry
articles.summary: In a revealing documentary, a looksmaxxing-influenced world where ‘your social capital is tied to your appearance’ has led to more men wanting more. Man’s obsession with his member is a tale as old as time, writ large in sky-scraping edifices, in allusions that flatter (big dick energy) or offend…
body: “A lot of the stories I worked on at those places were kind of fringy subculture and oftentimes adjacent to white nationalism,” says Lombroso, who became aware of the rising demand for penile enhancement procedures while reporting on plastic surgery trends at the New Yorker. “I started calling all these practitioners. But to make an embedded film the way I do, you need someone who’s very open.”

A 2024 study of US Google searches noted an increase in interest in penile-enhancement injections from 2013 through 2022. Lombroso’s 90-minute film, Manhood, puts male self-esteem issues at the heart of the trend on a cold, chafing examination table. Our guide throughout is Bill Moore, a capitalist in scrubs who gives fresh meaning to the phrase bedside manner. We meet him at home, tongue-kissing a pet lap dog while snuggled up under the covers with his male partner. We behold the full splendor of his naked body, nipped and tucked in retreat from the ravages of time and his own unforgiving eye. “Nobody would suspect I’ve ever had anything done!” he says with bracing cluelessness.

articles.title: ‘Green Room’ Director Recalls How Patrick Stewart “Saved” Movie From Being Scrapped
articles.summary: Ahead of a screening of the film on Friday, Jeremy Saulnier recounted how 'Green Room' was "close to shutting down" when the sci-fi icon, "out of the blue, expressed interest in the project."
body: Green Room director Jeremy Saulnier paid tribute to Patrick Stewart ahead of a Los Angeles screening of the film on Friday, recalling how the sci-fi icon “just swooped down, nosedived into our cruddy ass movie and saved us.”
Celebrating the film’s 10th anniversary, Saulnier addressed the crowd and noted Stewart’s death at 86.

The director remembered how production on Green Room was “at the point of no return, building sets, and under the gun without Darcy,” noting that the lead character of Darcy Banker had not yet been cast. However, that’s when the Star Trek star came in.

“We’re fucked, and we were close to shutting down. And Patrick Stewart, out of the blue, sort of expressed interest in the project,” Saulnier said. “And in a whirlwind, about a week later, I was on the phone with him. I left the stage [thinking,] ‘Maybe we’re gonna have to break down the sets and shut the whole movie down.’ Instead, this dude came out of nowhere, from way above our sort of zone, and just swooped down, nosedived into our cruddy ass movie and saved us, and said yes. And the movie was instantly greenlit.”

articles.title: Trump Lawsuit Against Wall Street Journal Over Epstein Story Dismissed by Judge
articles.summary: U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the suit with prejudice, ruling that the president did not prove the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice as required by law.
body: Saying the president was “grasping at straws,” a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump ’s $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
When a case is thrown out “with prejudice,” it cannot be refiled again and the dismissal is permanent and incontrovertible.

The dismissal is a blow to Trump and his administration, which have both pursued adversarial relationships with news organizations during his second term. In addition to the Journal, he is embroiled in lawsuits involving the BBC, The Associated Press and — most recently — CNN, MS NOW and Politico, which are suing him for restored access after he banished them from the White House in mid-September.
Trump has denounced media outlets that write things to which he objects and frequently calls them “fake news” and insults their journalists.

articles.title: Stephen King Has 2 Wildly Different 2026 Movie Recommendations That You Can Stream
articles.summary: Horror icon Stephen King has recommended two 2026 movies that could not be more different in tone and execution - and neither of them is a horror film.
body: On his Twitter/X account, bestselling author Stephen King mentioned two 2026 movies that he was very, very fond of. When a user recommended Kyle Balda's delightful murder mystery "The Sheep Detectives," King responded by saying that he loved it. "Sheep don't die," he wrote, "they turn into clouds," making a reference to the sheep's religious beliefs from the movie. King then immediately matched the user's recommendation by recommending Ben Wheatley's action thriller "Normal," starring Bob Odenkirk. "It's like 'Fargo' Lite," King wrote.

"The Sheep Detectives" and "Normal" couldn't be more different. The former is twee, delightful, and surprisingly thoughtful about death and mourning, especially for a film aimed at an audience of children. In the world of "The Sheep Detectives," sheep have a talent for deliberately forgetting anything unpleasant that's happened to them, a talent they must forego when their shepherd (Hugh Jackman) is murdered. The ovine sleuths have to find ways to alert the local constabulary to clues as to whodunnit. It's a sweet, cozy mystery that doesn't always shy away from the darker parts of a traditional film noir.
points: Horror icon Stephen King has recommended two 2026 movies that could not be more different in tone and execution - and neither of them is a horror film.

articles.title: It: Welcome To Derry Halloween Episode Features Live-Action Debut Of Iconic Stephen King Character
articles.summary: It: Welcome to Derry's special Halloween prequel episode features the very first on-screen appearance of a powerful, iconic Stephen King character.
body: Spoilers follow for the "It: Welcome to Derry" prequel episode "A Story of Derry."

This Halloween brought a surprise from HBO Max: a special prequel episode of "It: Welcome to Derry." Set hundreds of years before the main series, "A Story of Derry" is an extended version of the origin story that was sketched out in "Welcome to Derry" Episode 4. Kiawentiio ("Avatar: The Last Airbender") plays the lead character, Necina, a Shokopiwah youngster who unwisely decides to go hunting in the forbidden Western Wood. There, she and her friends learn the hard way that the stories about the evil that lurks in the trees are true.

While the episode doesn't add too much "Welcome to Derry" lore that we didn't already know, it does something that no other Stephen King adaptation (and there have been a lot of them) has done before. It shows Maturin, the cosmic space turtle, in all his glory on screen for the first time.

articles.title: Heidi Klum Reveals This Year’s (Very Bloody) Halloween Costume
articles.summary: The star transformed into a severed hand for her famous Halloween party on Saturday night.
body: It wouldn’t be Halloween without Heidi Klum, as the star revealed yet another jaw-dropping costume at her signature party on Saturday night.
The Queen of Halloween, as she has become known, celebrated the 25th anniversary of her NYC Halloween party this year, and Klum took it to the next level as she showed up as a severed hand.

Klum is hosting the event, presented by Apothic and Butterfinger, at Cathédrale Restaurant at Moxy East Village. The party has become one of Spooky Season’s most iconic events, as Klum always turns up in an elaborate look — in recent years, she’s transformed into Medusa, E.T., a peacock, Fiona from Shrek, Jessica Rabbit and famously, a worm.

The supermodel has been teasing glimpses at her costume on her Instagram, teasing her transformation all day long while asking her followers to submit their guesses on what she would become. Klum collaborates on her costumes with special effects makeup designer Mike Marino, who won an Emmy for his work on The Penguin. Marino revealed in a recent interview that “this costume this year is one of the most elaborate costumes ever made. It’s so difficult to do and just the complication of it is really challenging.”
